Observe that any dense open of <MATH_0001> contains the points <MATH_0002>
so the construction makes sense. To prove (1) or (2)
we may replace <MATH_0003> by any dense open. Thus if <MATH_0004>
are the irreducible components of <MATH_0005>, then we may replace
<MATH_0006> by <MATH_0007>.
After doing this <MATH_0008> is the disjoint union of its irreducible
components (viewed as open and closed subschemes). Then both the
right hand side and the left hand side of the arrow are products
over the irreducible components and we reduce to the case where
<MATH_0009> is irreducible.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Assume <MATH_0010> is irreducible with generic point <MATH_0011> lying over <MATH_0012>.
Part (1) follows from part (1) of
Lemma <REF_0001>.
Parts (2) and (3) follow from part (2) of the same lemma.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. A <TEXTITOPEN_0001>rational function on <MATH_0002><TEXTITCLOSE_0001> is a rational map
from <MATH_0003> to <MATH_0004>.

<STRUCT_0001>
See Constructions, Definition <REF_0001>
for the definition of the affine line <MATH_0001>. Let <MATH_0002> be a scheme
over <MATH_0003>. For any open <MATH_0004> a morphism
<MATH_0005> is the same as a morphism
<MATH_0006> over <MATH_0007>. Hence a rational function is
also the same as a <MATH_0008>-rational map from <MATH_0009> into <MATH_0010>.

Recall that we have the canonical identification
<MATH_0011>
for any scheme <MATH_0012>, see Schemes, Example <REF_0002>.
Hence <MATH_0013> is a ring-object in the
category of schemes. More precisely, the morphisms
<MATH_0014>
satisfy all the axioms of the addition and multiplication in a ring
(commutative with <MATH_0015> as always). Hence also the set of rational
maps into <MATH_0016> has a natural ring structure.
